add.issue.comment.md:
Fork (decision: operator, 2026-10-06): the script is not a wrapper around the Aphotic installer. It is shaped like the community-scripts Proxmox VE Helper (community-scripts.org): it runs on the PVE host itself and provides a default and an advanced install function for Proxmox, plus the dev VM lifecycle.

- init: writes a commented ~/.config/aphotic/devvm.env; every host/VM value comes from that file; the example carries no value pointing at anyone's network.
- install: Proxmox VE on a bare Debian host. default = no-subscription repo, PVE kernel, CPU microcode. advanced = --enterprise, --bridge, --ip/--gateway/--dns.
- create-vm: the dev VM from the latest Arch opencloud image. default = the machine that runs a real Hyprland session (q35, OVMF, host CPU, VirtIO-GPU render node, 12 GiB / 6 cores / 60 GiB, cloud-init user + SSH key, DHCP). advanced = one flag per setting (--vmid, --name, --machine, --cpu, --cores, --ram, --disk, --display, --bridge, --storage, --mac, --vlan, --mtu, --user, --ssh-key, --ip, --gateway, --dns, --no-start).
- reset / destroy / status: the dev VM lifecycle, so a failed test is minutes from a clean slate.

Nothing in the script is specific to the Aphotic installer; booting the desktop and running the installer inside the VM are manual steps the docs describe.

Found while writing the Dev-VM guide (5NEQQW0): Arch has retired the opencloud images. https://archlinux.org/releng/cloud/ is a 404, the ~arch-releng/images/ mirror directories are gone, and the latest release (2026.10.01) ships only ISOs and the bootstrap tarball. The create-vm path in PR #299 downloaded from that dead page, so it would have failed on any real host.

Fixed in 1b33903 (PR #299 updated): create-vm now follows the community-scripts helper convention it is modelled on. It downloads the latest installer ISO from the official mirror (https://geo.mirror.pkgbuild.com/iso/latest/archlinux-x86_64.iso, overridable with --iso-url / DEVVM_ISO_URL), imports it as the VM's boot disk, grows the disk to the configured size, and boots the live environment. The base system is then installed once in the guest console with archinstall (user, sudo, SSH key, plus openssh and qemu-guest-agent in the package list), which the wiki Dev-VM page documents for both libvirt and Proxmox.

Cloud-init is gone from the VM path with it: the --ip/--gateway/--dns VM options are deleted (they only worked through cloud-init), and status says when the guest agent is not up yet. tools/ci/local.sh is green in the worktree (75 bash files, 238 pytest, shellcheck advisory only). Still not verified on a real PVE host; the ISO URL and the import-as-boot-disk trick are the parts a first real run should confirm.

add.issue.comment.md:
**Method: read which DRM card Hyprland has open, map it to the PCI bus ID. Verified live on a hybrid box (iGPU Intel UHD 770 + RTX 4090, Hyprland 0.56.2, desktop compositing on the iGPU).**

1. **Hyprland PID.** `hyprctl -j instances` returns `[{instance, pid, wl_socket}]`; the shell matches `instance` against its own `HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE` env var (set by `aphotic-shell.service`), so it is unambiguous with multiple Hyprland instances. `pidof Hyprland` as fallback.
2. **The compositor's card.** Scan `/proc/<pid>/fd` for `/dev/dri/card*` symlinks, dedupe (Hyprland holds several fds per card: six on `card1` on this box). Here Hyprland (pid 2393) holds `card1` (Intel) fds and none on `card0` (4090) -> the desktop composites on the iGPU.
3. **Map to the PCI bus ID** (the key the VRAM resources / Flow v2 will use): `basename $(readlink /sys/class/drm/card1/device)` -> `0000:00:02.0`. Render nodes resolve identically (`/sys/class/drm/renderD129` sits under the same PCI device), so a `renderD*`-only fd set also works; prefer `card*` fds.
4. **Decision.** nvidia-smi `pci.bus_id` (`00000000:01:00.0` -> strip leading zeros -> `0000:01:00.0`); AMD and Intel cards resolve through the same sysfs basename. Loaded card in the compositor's card set -> `minimal`, else `abstract`. On this box: compositor `0000:00:02.0`, load `0000:01:00.0` -> different -> `abstract`.

Why the ticket's other candidates don't carry it:
- **`AQ_DRM_DEVICES`** (set to `/dev/dri/card1` on this box): Hyprland injects it only into the environment of processes it spawns itself. It is absent from Hyprland's own environ and from the shell's, because the shell is started by `aphotic-shell.service` (systemd user unit, `ExecStart=/usr/bin/qs -c aphotic`), not by Hyprland. Usable only if the shell happens to be a Hyprland child (exec-once/manual start).
- **`hyprctl` output**: `systeminfo` lists all GPUs (lspci dump), not the one that composites; 0.56.2 has no hyprctl command reporting the rendering GPU. `hyprctl instances` is only useful for the PID.

Topologies:
- **Single-GPU box**: one card, always shared -> `minimal`. Same code path.
- **Hybrid laptop**: Hyprland composites on the dGPU (prime) or the iGPU (offload); the fd scan reports whatever is actually open, including both cards when probe/offload fds are held. Set semantics ("shared only if the loaded card is among the opened ones") avoid false confidence.
- **iGPU + dGPU desktop** (this box): compositor on the iGPU, 4090 under load -> `abstract`. Verified.

Caveats:
- Never infer from the shell's own fds: on this box `qs` itself opens `renderD128` (the 4090; Qt picks the dGPU for its own windows) while the desktop composites on the iGPU. A child's render node is not the compositor's.
- The `/dev/dri/dgpu` / `/dev/dri/igpu` symlinks on this box come from a machine-local udev rule with hardcoded PCI IDs; not a portable signal.
- `LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=iHD` in Hyprland children is a corroborating hint (the VA driver follows the GPU Hyprland picked), not a method.
- Same-user `/proc` access is guaranteed (shell and Hyprland both run as the desktop user).

add.issue.comment.md:
**First step: coverage measurement.** The shell renders **177 distinct Material Symbol ligature names** (extracted from every `MaterialIcon` `text:` site, `icon:`/`glyph:` property defaults, the `Icons.qml` helper returns, the category/weather icon maps, and the app-icon fallback args). Six MIT/ISC-licensed line candidates were measured against that vocabulary: exact name match, plus a curated conceptual alias where naming conventions differ (every alias verified to exist in the set's official name list; Remix Icon excluded as Apache-2.0).

| Set (license) | Set size | exact | aliased | coverage |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lucide (ISC) | 1866 | 43 | 121 | **164/177 (93%)** |
| Phosphor (MIT) | 1512 | 33 | 124 | **157/177 (89%)** |
| Tabler (MIT) | 5184 | 47 | 109 | **156/177 (88%)** |
| Feather (MIT) | 287 | 32 | 89 | 121/177 (68%) |
| Iconoir (MIT) | 1383 | 31 | 81 | 112/177 (63%) |
| Majesticons (MIT) | 380 | 21 | 66 | 87/177 (49%) |

Notes:
- Phosphor's name vocabulary is identical across all six weights (the "9000 icons" figure is 1512 names x 6 weights). Its **thin** weight is the only true hairline stroke in the group; Lucide, Tabler and Feather are standard 2px line weight (Lucide's stroke is adjustable at render time).
- The aliased column is the size of the hand-written name map the plan already budgets for ("add a name map so call sites keep working").
- The uncovered remainders are dominated by: wifi bar-strength variants (Feather/Iconoir/Majesticons have no per-bar icons), keyboard key badges (capslock/alt/command), layout-specific glyphs (`dock_to_*`, `space_bar`, `rounded_corner`, `looks_one`, `vertical_align_bottom`), and a few concepts no candidate has at all (`deployed_code_alert`, `release_alert`, `smart_toy`, `dialpad`, `dns`, `ac_unit` depending on set).
- Lucide leads on coverage (93%) and is ISC; Phosphor is a close second (89%) and the only set with a hairline-weight option matching "stroke matches the hairline weight"; Tabler is the largest set (5184) and leaves the most headroom for custom app-icon "glyph" kind.
- The three leaders sit within ~5 points of each other, so the choice likely turns on stroke weight (Phosphor thin vs 2px) and font packaging rather than on coverage. The 177-name vocabulary and the per-set alias table can be posted on request.

add.issue.comment.md:
Pi and OMP are wired; Dsh is untouched (no adapter in this work).

Design: one adapter (pi-hooks plugin) serves both harnesses, because both run the pi-mono extension API -- pi under Node, OMP under its embedded Bun. It maps extension events to the v2 contract (session/turn/tool lifecycle, per-response usage, quota windows) into the core writer; no core writer change was needed. Core registers omp+pi in AgentRoles/AgentProviders; no pgrep reconcile for either, since pi's comm is node and OMP's never matches, so the event tail is their only presence source.

Quota: context fill from the runtime on both harnesses; OMP adds provider windows (fiveHour/sevenDay) from agent.db usage_history for the session's own provider. Pi has none -- honest context-only gap.

Verified: live concurrent pi -p + omp -p through the real writer (full lifecycle both, live context fill, tool events, end events); 8 adapter tests + sandboxed wire round trip (symlink for pi, shim file for OMP whose discovery scan skips symlinks); v2 contract fixtures in core; headless qs probe over the recorded feed proving the notch/bar consumer stack serves pi+omp usage, quota and labels.

PRs (open, unmerged): T-Crypt/aphotic-hypr#305 (core, base dev), T-Crypt/aphotic-plugins#44 (plugin, base main).
